summary_en: Growth xPartners changed its dividend policy to distribute earnings after securing funds for growth investment and working capital. The company will pay an initial dividend of 22 yen per share for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, targeting a payout ratio of around 20% and DOE of 2.0% as a lower bound for stable dividends, with plans to gradually raise the payout ratio to over 30% within three years.
title_en: Notice Regarding Change in Dividend Policy and Distribution of Retained Earnings (Initial Dividend)
translation_en_brief:
Growth xPartners announced a change in its dividend policy on October 15, 2026, shifting from a no-dividend stance adopted since listing to an approach that prioritizes growth investment while distributing surplus cash to shareholders. The company will implement its first dividend of 22 yen per share for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, to be approved at the shareholders' meeting scheduled for November 26, 2026, with an effective date of November 27, 2026. This initial dividend will result in a consolidated payout ratio of 18.5% and a DOE of 2.0%.

Under the new policy, the company targets a payout ratio of approximately 20% as a guideline, with DOE of 2.0% as the lower bound for stable dividends. The company plans to gradually increase the payout ratio to over 30% within three years, subject to the progress of growth investments and business performance. The policy reflects management's judgment that the company's financial foundation is already at an appropriate level, with sufficient liquidity remaining to support growth investments even after the dividend payment.

The company emphasized that growth investment is the top priority in capital allocation. Beyond traditional M&A-driven business expansion, the company intends to diversify investments toward human capital, technology infrastructure, research and development, and strategic partnerships and collaborations. This strategy shift is tied to the company's transformation into a "business transformation partner" amid the rapid proliferation of generative AI, for which it is establishing a new subsidiary focused on strategic consulting.
